text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like TSLA on 2026-09-18, the realised 20-session return had a median of 2.96% and a mean of 2.39%. The distribution is slightly left-skewed, with 68% of analogs finishing above zero and 32% below. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -3.53%, because in these conditions the intra-horizon drawdown was typically worse than the terminal return.

[state]
The retrieval engine pulled these 50 analogs from 39 distinct sessions across 30 symbols because the current state combines several distinctive features: a 5d/20d volatility ratio of 0.489 (z-score -1.217), meaning short-term vol has collapsed relative to the month; a WTI crude change over 20 days of 19.24% (z-score 1.124); a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score of -1.558 (used at -1.026), indicating thin liquidity; 20-session realised volatility of 48.97% (z-score 0.983); and a distance from the 52-week high of -26.98% (z-score -0.841). The macro backdrop shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a Fed funds target change over 90 days of 0.25 bp. Equity market sentiment sits at a score of 57.1 in the "Greed" band, though the CNN Business Fear & Greed cross-check reads 38.3, rated "fear", driven by extreme fear in stock price strength and breadth. For TSLA specifically, Yahoo Finance headlines note that "Tesla Stock Rises Overnight After Musk Says ‘Something May Come Of’ TSMC Talks On Terafab" and that "Nvidia, Tesla Shares Head for 24/7 Onchain Trading Under OKX and NYSE Owner’s Venture". The crypto sentiment reading of 70 ("Greed") and crypto headlines apply only to the separate tokenised wrapper market, not to the equity's mood.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the 20-session forward returns range from -11.47% to 15.49%, with a standard deviation of 6.9%. The 10th percentile is -8.68% and the 90th percentile is 10.51%. The skew is -0.288, meaning the left tail is slightly fatter. In 18 of the 50 cases the return fell below -5%, and in 4 it fell below -10%. The worst outcomes are dominated by specific episodes: Li Auto ADR (LI) on 2025-09-22 returned -11.47% with a max adverse excursion of -13.16%; Boeing (BA) on 2021-08-04 returned -3.76% but suffered a -6.92% drawdown along the way. The best outcomes include Schlumberger (SLB) on 2026-08-04 returning 12.48%, Nike (NKE) on 2023-10-10 returning 12.03%, and the single TSLA analog itself (2025-08-07) returning 8.87%. Technology names make up 12 of the 50 analogs, and China ADRs account for 7.

[tails]
A position can finish near its starting point while being un-holdable through the middle. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs is -3.53%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reaches -10.99%, and at the 25th percentile it is -7.38%. Conversely, the median max favourable excursion is 6.73%, reaching 14.07% at the 90th percentile, giving a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.91. In terms of breach probabilities, 40% of the analog paths experienced a 5% drawdown at some point during the 20 sessions, 14% breached a 10% drawdown, and none breached 15% or 20%.

[stress]
The baseline median return is 2.96%. The stress scenarios that materially worsen this picture are the rate and inflation regimes. The 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario produced a median forward return of -7.83% (a delta of -10.79% versus baseline) across 50 analogs, with a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yielded a median of -6.29% (delta -9.25%) across 50 analogs, with a 50% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash showed a median of -3.2% (delta -6.16%) across 48 analogs, with a 72.9% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock gave a median of -0.86% (delta -3.82%) across 26 analogs, with a 61.5% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The earnings release day scenario produced a median of -1.18% (delta -4.14%) across 50 analogs, with a 48% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue scenario resulted in a median of 2.62% (delta -0.34%) across 50 analogs, with a 14% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count—a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution—and the measured window holds only a handful of distinct weekends, so blocks are cross-correlated. No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the 2022 inflation / rate bear (median -7.83%, delta -10.79%, 50 analogs, 74% breach probability) because the current state includes elevated oil prices and a steep curve that historically compressed multiples; the 2018-Q4 tightening scare (median -6.29%, delta -9.25%, 50 analogs, 50% breach probability) because it isolates rate-driven de-rating without an earnings collapse; and the earnings release day scenario (median -1.18%, delta -4.14%, 50 analogs, 48% breach probability) because the card notes 45 calendar days to the next earnings release, placing an event directly inside the 20-session horizon. A concentration to distrust is the year 2025, which accounts for 20 of the 50 analogs, potentially overweighting recent regime dynamics. None of the stress scenarios contradict the direction of a positive baseline median, but the regional bank stress (2023-03) and China ADR de-rating scenarios actually produced positive medians (3.07% and 1% respectively), showing that not all shocks penalise this specific feature set.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The honest verdict from the engine's validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The conformal interval achieves 87.4% out-of-sample coverage against an 80% target, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name benchmark is -3.4%. The path risk validation shows that at the stated 10% drawdown level, the realised breach rate out of sample was 16.2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 17.2%, yielding a calibration gap of 1.03 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 2.47. The Brier score of the analog MAE is 0.1335. Against the volatility reflection benchmark (0.136), the paired difference confidence interval spans zero (-0.0144 to 0.0102), meaning it is unresolved. Against the same-name calibration (0.1333), the interval also spans zero (-0.0087 to 0.0097), so it is unresolved. Against the pooled calibration (0.1378), the interval does not span zero (-0.0128 to 0.0041), resolving in favour of the analog. Regarding the tokenised wrapper, the status is "measured" on the primary venue, Bitget official MCP (TSLA/USDT, an RWA perpetual). The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 44.55% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. The tracking tier is "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9637 and a tracking error of 98 bp/day. The basis band is -0.51% to 0.39%, and the spread is 0.26 bps. The wrapper caveat notes that a fair perpetual is not the underlying, carries funding, and the basis means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. The closed-session return layer, measured on 6 distinct weekend starts (pooled across 39 instruments, so not independent draws), shows a median weekend block return of -0.312%, a 10th percentile of -1.13%, a standard deviation of 1.0081%, and a median intra-weekend adverse excursion of -0.6715%. Zero percent of those 6 weekend blocks breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
